h.en: 1.1 The theodolite — introduction, uses and parts

items.syllabus_item: 1.1 Introduction to theodolite, uses, sketch and parts of Transit Vernier theodolite

body.en:
What it is. The theodolite is the surveyor's angle instrument: a telescope mounted so it can rotate in both the horizontal and vertical planes over graduated circles, reading angles to 20 seconds in a vernier instrument (1 second or better in digital/micro-optic ones). Everything else in this subject — traverse, tacheometry, curve setting — is the theodolite pointed at a new problem.

Uses. Measuring horizontal and vertical angles; setting out angles and alignments; prolonging and ranging lines; measuring magnetic bearings; optical distance measurement (tacheometry, Unit 2); levelling when used as a level; and laying out curves (Unit 3). Parts to name on sight (Diagram): telescope with internal focussing, vertical circle with vernier, standards (A-frames), upper plate carrying the verniers and plate bubbles, lower plate carrying the horizontal circle, clamps and tangent (slow-motion) screws for each plate, levelling head with three foot screws on a tribrach, shifting head for centering, and the tripod. In a transit theodolite the telescope can be flipped completely about the trunnion axis — the property Unit 1 exploits for face-left/face-right work.
body.gu:
પરિચય: Theodolite એ surveyor નું angle માપવાનું instrument છે — telescope એવી રીતે mount થયેલું હોય છે કે તે horizontal અને vertical બંને plane માં ફરી શકે અને graduated circle પર vernier થી 20 second સુધી angle વાંચી શકાય. આ subject નું બીજું બધું — traverse, tacheometry, curve setting — એ theodolite ને નવા problem તરફ તાકવા જેવું જ છે.

ઉપયોગ: horizontal અને vertical angle માપવા, angle અને alignment set out કરવો, line prolong અને range કરવી, magnetic bearing માપવો, optical distance માપવો (tacheometry), levelling અને curve layout. Parts (Diagram માં જુઓ): telescope, vertical circle, standards (A-frame), vernier અને plate bubble ધરાવતી upper plate, horizontal circle ધરાવતી lower plate, clamp અને tangent screw, ત્રણ foot screw વાળું levelling head, tribrach, shifting head અને tripod. Transit theodolite માં telescope trunnion axis પર સંપૂર્ણ flip થઈ શકે છે — એ જ property face-left/face-right માટે વપરાય છે.

h.en: 1.2 Reading the main and vernier scales
h.gu: 1.2 Main scale અને vernier scale reading

items.syllabus_item: 1.2 Reading of main and vernier scale on horizontal and vertical plate

body.en:
Why a vernier. The horizontal and vertical circles are graduated in degrees, usually to 20 minutes (one-third of a degree) per smallest main-scale division — far too coarse for traverse work. The vernier plate subdivides that division optically: 60 vernier divisions are made equal to 59 main divisions, so the least count is one-sixtieth of 20 minutes = 20 seconds (Diagram, Numerical 1.1).

least count = (1 main-scale division)/(number of vernier divisions) = 20 min/60 = 20 sec

How to read. (1) Read the main scale up to the division just before the vernier zero (index) — degrees and 20-minute steps. (2) Find the one vernier line that coincides exactly with a main-scale line; multiply its number by 20 seconds. (3) Add the two. Two verniers (A and B) sit 180° apart on the plate; averaging A and B readings cancels eccentricity error of the circle. The vertical circle is read the same way, with its own vernier and index error checked against the altitude bubble. Reading discipline: shade the circle, use the magnifier, call degrees–minutes–seconds aloud, and book A and B separately — most angle blunders are born here, not in the field geometry.
body.gu:
Vernier શા માટે: circle પર degree ના ભાગ પડેલા હોય છે, સામાન્ય રીતે સૌથી નાનો main-scale division = 20 minute — traverse માટે એ બહુ મોટો છે. Vernier plate એ division ને 60 ભાગમાં વહેંચે છે (60 vernier division = 59 main division), એટલે least count = 20 minute/60 = 20 second (Diagram, Numerical 1.1).

least count = (1 main-scale division)/(vernier divisions) = 20 min/60 = 20 sec

Reading રીત: (1) vernier zero (index) પહેલાનો main-scale division વાંચો — degree અને 20-minute steps. (2) જે vernier line main-scale line સાથે બરાબર coincide થાય તેનો number × 20 second. (3) બંને ઉમેરો. Plate પર 180° દૂર A અને B બે vernier હોય છે; બંનેનું mean લેવાથી circle ની eccentricity error cancel થાય છે. Vertical circle પણ આવી જ રીતે વંચાય છે.

body.en:
Temporary adjustment = the ritual at every station, in this order. (1) Setting up and centering: tripod legs spread firmly, instrument roughly level by eye, plumb bob (or optical plummet) brought exactly over the station peg by shifting the legs and then the shifting head — centering to within 1–2 mm. (2) Levelling up: with the plate bubble over two foot screws, turn both screws equally in or out until the bubble centres; rotate 90° and centre with the third screw alone; repeat until the bubble stays central in both positions (and ideally through a full swing). (3) Focussing: eyepiece first — sight a white paper/sky and turn the eyepiece until the cross-hairs are razor sharp; then objective focussing on the target until image and cross-hairs show no parallax (they must not separate when the eye moves).

Why the order matters. Centering after levelling disturbs the level; focussing before levelling wastes nothing but parallax left in the system becomes a pointing error at every target. In traverse work you repeat this ritual at every station of the polygon (Card 1.10), so professionals make it muscle memory: legs–centre–level–focus, every time, without thinking.
body.gu:
Temporary adjustment = દરેક station પરની ક્રિયા, આ જ ક્રમમાં: (1) Centering: tripod મજબૂત ગોઠવો, plumb bob અથવા optical plummet station peg પર બરાબર લાવો — પહેલા leg ખસેડી, પછી shifting head થી fine centering (1–2 mm માં). (2) Levelling: plate bubble બે foot screw ઉપર રાખી બંને screw સરખા ફેરવી bubble centre માં લાવો; 90° ફેરવી ત્રીજા screw થી centre કરો; bubble બંને position માં centre રહે ત્યાં સુધી repeat કરો. (3) Focussing: પહેલા eyepiece થી cross-hair sharp કરો, પછી objective focussing કરી parallax દૂર કરો — આંખ ખસેડવાથી image અને cross-hair અલગ ન પડવા જોઈએ.

ક્રમ કેમ મહત્વનો છે: levelling પછી centering કરશો તો level બગડશે; parallax રહી જશે તો દરેક target પર pointing error આવશે. Traverse માં આ ક્રિયા દરેક station પર repeat થાય છે, એટલે legs–centre–level–focus યાદ રાખો.

h.en: 1.4 Permanent adjustment and the fundamental axes

items.syllabus_item: 1.4 Permanent adjustment of theodolite (fundamental axes and their relationship)

body.en:
Four axes, three relationships (Diagram). The instrument carries a vertical axis (the spindle about which the telescope rotates horizontally), a trunnion (horizontal) axis (about which the telescope flips vertically), the line of collimation (objective-to-cross-hair line, the actual sighting line), and the axis of the plate bubble. In perfect adjustment: plate-bubble axis ⊥ vertical axis; line of collimation ⊥ trunnion axis; trunnion axis ⊥ vertical axis; (plus the vertical-circle index reads zero when the telescope is horizontal, and the altitude bubble axis is parallel to collimation).

Permanent adjustments restore these when workshop/field tests fail: plate-bubble adjustment (bubble stays centred through 180° swing), collimation adjustment (spire test / two-peg style reversal test), trunnion-axis adjustment (high-point spire test), and vertical-circle index adjustment. The trainee's takeaway: permanent adjustment is done rarely and carefully — but observing on both faces (Card 1.6) hides a sick instrument's errors, which is why field procedure, not the workshop, saves most surveys.
body.gu:
ચાર axes, ત્રણ સંબંધ (Diagram): instrument માં vertical axis (જેની આસપાસ telescope horizontal માં ફરે), trunnion (horizontal) axis (જેની આસપાસ telescope vertical માં flip થાય), line of collimation (objective થી cross-hair — ખરી sighting line) અને plate bubble axis હોય છે. Perfect adjustment માં: bubble axis ⊥ vertical axis; collimation ⊥ trunnion axis; trunnion axis ⊥ vertical axis.

Permanent adjustment આ સંબંધો test માં fail થાય ત્યારે પાછા લાવે છે: plate-bubble adjustment, collimation adjustment (spire test), trunnion-axis adjustment અને vertical-circle index adjustment. Permanent adjustment ભાગ્યે જ થાય છે — પણ બંને face પર observation લેવાથી ખરાબ instrument ની error પણ છુપાઈ જાય છે, એટલે field procedure જ મોટાભાગના survey બચાવે છે.

h.en: 1.5 Technical terms you must be fluent in
h.gu: 1.5 Technical terms — જે શબ્દો સ્પષ્ટ હોવા જોઈએ

body.en:
The working vocabulary. Centering — vertical axis exactly over the station. Face left / face right — vertical circle on the observer's left/right of the telescope; changing face = transiting plus rotating 180°. Transiting (plunging) — flipping the telescope 180° about the trunnion axis. Swinging — rotating the telescope horizontally (right swing = clockwise from above). Telescope normal / inverted — bubble up versus transited position. Line of sight / collimation — the optical line through objective centre and cross-hair intersection. Station — the marked ground point occupied or observed. Back sight / fore sight — sight to the previous / next traverse station. Closing the horizon — summing angles around a point to check 360° (Card 1.6).

Why definitions are examinable. Half of theodolite viva questions are definition traps (transiting vs swinging, face change vs swing). Each term names one physical motion or state of the instrument — learn them by pointing at the instrument and doing the motion, not by cramming sentences.
body.gu:
મુખ્ય શબ્દો: Centering — vertical axis બરાબર station ઉપર. Face left / face right — vertical circle observer ની ડાબી/જમણી બાજુએ; face બદલવો = transiting + 180° rotation. Transiting — telescope ને trunnion axis પર 180° flip કરવો. Swinging — telescope ને horizontal માં ફેરવવો. Line of sight / collimation — objective centre અને cross-hair માંથી પસાર થતી optical line. Station — જમીન પર mark કરેલો point. Back sight / fore sight — અગાઉના / આગલા station તરફની sight. Closing the horizon — એક point આસપાસના બધા angle નો સરવાળો 360° check કરવો.

કેમ મહત્વના છે: theodolite viva ના અડધા પ્રશ્નો definition પર જ હોય છે (transiting vs swinging). દરેક શબ્દ instrument ની એક physical motion કે state છે — instrument પર motion કરીને શીખો.

h.gu: 1.6 Horizontal angle અને vertical angle માપવા

items.syllabus_item: 1.6 Methods of measuring horizontal angles and vertical angles

body.en:
Horizontal angle — three field methods. (1) Ordinary/direct method: bisect back station, read; bisect fore station, read; difference = angle; repeat on the other face and mean. (2) Repetition method: add the same angle 3–6 times around the circle, divide the total by the number of repetitions — graduation and reading errors shrink by that factor, giving 20″/n precision from a 20″ instrument; the standard for traverse angles. (3) Reiteration (direction) method: observe all angles around a station in sequence, closing the horizon at 360°, distribute the misclosure, then swing back on the other face — best when many lines radiate from one station.

Vertical angle. Sight the target, read the vertical circle with the altitude bubble/index correct; angle of elevation is positive up, depression negative. Observe face left and face right and mean them to kill index error. Booking discipline decides accuracy more than the instrument: read both verniers, check the horizon closure (≤ n×least count), and never accept an angle set whose two faces differ wildly — re-observe, do not 'adjust' blunders away.
body.gu:
Horizontal angle — ત્રણ field methods: (1) Ordinary method: back station bisect કરી reading, fore station bisect કરી reading; તફાવત = angle; બંને face નું mean લો. (2) Repetition method: એ જ angle 3–6 વખત circle પર ઉમેરતા જાઓ, કુલ ને repetition સંખ્યાથી ભાગો — reading error એટલા ભાગમાં ઘટે છે; traverse angle માટે standard method. (3) Reiteration method: station આસપાસના બધા angle ક્રમમાં માપો, horizon 360° પર close કરો, misclosure વહેંચો — ઘણી line એક station થી નીકળતી હોય ત્યારે શ્રેષ્ઠ.

Vertical angle: target bisect કરી vertical circle reading લો (elevation +, depression −); બંને face નું mean index error cancel કરે છે. Accuracy instrument કરતાં booking discipline પર વધુ આધારિત છે: બંને vernier વાંચો, horizon closure check કરો.

h.en: 1.7 Magnetic bearing, prolonging a line, ranging a line
h.gu: 1.7 Magnetic bearing માપવો, line prolong કરવી, line range કરવી

items.syllabus_item: 1.7 Use theodolite to measure magnetic bearing, prolong a line, range a line

body.en:
Magnetic bearing. With the trough compass (or tubular compass) attached and the circle set to zero, release the needle and rotate the instrument until the needle centres against its marks — the telescope now points along magnetic north on face; bisect the target station and the circle reading is the magnetic bearing (whole-circle). Check on both faces and against a compass reading; local attraction betrays itself when fore and back bearings of the same line refuse to differ by 180°.

Prolonging a line. At the end station, back-sight the previous station, transit the telescope — the line of sight now extends the line forward; fix the new point, then repeat on the other face and take the mean of the two marked points (any split between them exposes collimation error). Double prolonging this way can carry a straight alignment for kilometres. Ranging a line is the inverse favour: given two end stations, set the theodolite on one, sight the other, and line in intermediate points so long offsets, chain lines or fence lines run truly straight between fixed ends.
body.gu:
Magnetic bearing: trough compass લગાવી circle zero પર રાખો, needle મુક્ત કરી instrument એવી રીતે ફેરવો કે needle magnetic north દર્શાવે; પછી target station bisect કરો — circle reading એ whole-circle magnetic bearing છે. બંને face પર check કરો; fore અને back bearing નો તફાવત 180° ન આવે તો local attraction છે.

Line prolong કરવી: છેલ્લું station પર અગાઉના station નું back sight લઈ telescope transit કરો — sight line આગળ લંબાય છે; નવો point mark કરો, બીજા face પર repeat કરી બંને point નું mean લો. Line range કરવી આનાથી ઊલટું છે: બે છેડાના station fixed હોય તો એક પર theodolite ગોઠવી બીજા તરફ sight કરી વચ્ચેના intermediate points સીધી line માં ગોઠવો.

body.en:
Direct angle. The clockwise angle from the back line (produced backwards to the previous station) to the fore line: set zero on the back station with the circle reading the back bearing if you like, swing clockwise to the fore station — the reading is the direct angle, and bearings propagate station to station by adding it. It is the workhorse of route traverses (roads, canals, pipelines) where the party walks the alignment.

Deflection angle. The small angle between the prolongation of the back line and the fore line — right (R) if the line turns clockwise, left (L) otherwise. A straight line has deflection 0°, a road curve begins exactly where deflection becomes non-zero — which is why Unit 3's Rankine method is nothing but deflection angles marched along chords. Field method: back-sight, transit (telescope now points along the prolonged line, circle reading flipped by 180°), then swing to the fore station; the small reading (or its supplement, handled carefully) is the deflection. Examiners love the R/L suffix: a deflection without its letter is only half an answer.
body.gu:
Direct angle: back station થી clockwise માપેલો fore station સુધીનો angle. Zero back station પર રાખી clockwise swing કરો — reading એ direct angle; bearing station-દર-station આગળ વધે છે. Road, canal, pipeline જેવા route traverse માં સૌથી વધુ વપરાય છે.

Deflection angle: back line ના prolongation (આગળ લંબાવેલી દિશા) અને fore line વચ્ચેનો નાનો angle — જમણે વળે તો R, ડાબે વળે તો L લખાય. સીધી line નો deflection = 0°; જ્યાંથી deflection શૂન્ય નથી ત્યાંથી curve શરૂ થાય છે — Unit 3 ની Rankine method આ જ deflection angle નો ઉપયોગ કરે છે. R/L letter વગરનો જવાબ અધૂરો ગણાય છે.

body.en:
Instrumental errors. Imperfect permanent adjustment (bubble, collimation, trunnion axis out — Card 1.4); eccentricity of circle and verniers (killed by reading A and B verniers and meaning); imperfect graduation (spread by repetition/reiteration over different circle parts); a bent or loose tripod/axis play. Cure hierarchy: adjust what you can, then observe so the rest cancels — face-left/face-right means remove collimation, trunnion tilt and index errors in one stroke.

Personal and natural errors. Personal: imperfect centering and levelling, careless bisection, parallax left in, reading/booking blunders (the commonest and the largest). Natural: wind shake, unequal heating of the instrument (sun on one standard), refraction shimmer at midday, tripod settlement into soft ground. Field defences are procedural: shade the instrument, observe in calm morning/evening light, re-centre checks between rounds, close the horizon, and re-observe anything that fails tolerance (angle closure for n stations: √n × least count is the usual yardstick). Errors you cannot remove, you must design the observation to cancel — that sentence is the whole philosophy of precise surveying.
body.gu:
Instrumental errors: permanent adjustment ખામી (bubble, collimation, trunnion axis), circle-vernier eccentricity (A અને B vernier નું mean લેવાથી cancel), graduation ખામી (repetition થી ઘટે), ઢીલો tripod. Face-left/face-right નું mean લેવાથી collimation, trunnion અને index error એકસાથે cancel થાય છે.

Personal અને natural errors: ખોટું centering/levelling, parallax, reading-booking ની ભૂલ (સૌથી સામાન્ય); પવન, તડકો, refraction, નરમ જમીનમાં tripod ખસવો. બચાવ: instrument ને છાંયડો આપો, શાંત સમયમાં observation લો, horizon close કરો, tolerance બહાર જાય તો ફરી observe કરો — error દૂર ન થાય તો observation એવી ગોઠવો કે error cancel જ થાય.

body.en:
What a traverse is. A framework of connected straight lines whose lengths are taped/chained (or measured by EDM/tacheometer later) and whose angles or bearings are measured with the theodolite: from one known point, direction + distance walks you to every new station (Diagram). Closed traverses (polygon returning to start, or link traverses closing on known points) carry their own error check; open traverses do not and are avoided for control work.

Four ways to run the directions. (1) Included-angle method — measure each polygon interior angle (repetition), check Σ = (2n − 4) × 90°, then compute bearings round the loop. (2) Fast-needle method — magnetic bearing of every line read directly with the compass attachment at each station; fast, but magnetic disturbances poison it. (3) Deflection-angle method — route surveys (Card 1.8). (4) Direct-angle/azimuth method — carry whole-circle bearings forward by direct angles. Field sequence per station is unchanging: center–level–focus, back sight, fore sight, both faces, book, move. The angles alone are not the survey — lengths measured twice (forward/back, agreeing to ~1 in 2000 for traverse work) complete each side.
body.gu:
Traverse એટલે શું: જોડાયેલી સીધી lines નું framework જેમાં દરેક line ની length tape થી અને angle/bearing theodolite થી માપવામાં આવે છે; એક known point થી direction + distance વડે દરેક નવા station પર પહોંચાય છે (Diagram). Closed traverse પોતાની error check ધરાવે છે; open traverse માં check નથી.

Direction ચલાવવાની રીતો: (1) Included-angle method — દરેક interior angle માપો, Σ = (2n − 4) × 90° check, પછી bearing ગણો. (2) Fast-needle method — દરેક station પર magnetic bearing સીધો વાંચો; ઝડપી પણ magnetic disturbance થી બગડે. (3) Deflection-angle method — route survey માટે. (4) Direct-angle method — whole-circle bearing આગળ લઈ જાઓ. દરેક station પર ક્રમ એક જ: centre–level–focus, back sight, fore sight, બંને face, booking, આગળ વધો.

h.en: 1.11 Traverse computations, closing error and balancing
h.gu: 1.11 Traverse computations, closing error અને balancing

items.syllabus_item: 1.11 Traverse computations, closing errors, balancing the traverse

body.en:
Latitude and departure resolve each line into north-south and east-west components from its whole-circle bearing θ and length L:

latitude = L cos(theta) ; departure = L sin(theta) (signs by quadrant of theta)

For a perfectly closed polygon Σlatitude = 0 and Σdeparture = 0. What remains is the closing error e = √( (Σlat)² + (Σdep)² ), quoted as relative accuracy e/perimeter (1 in 5000 is respectable diploma traverse work). Balancing distributes it before coordinates are computed: Bowditch (compass) rule — correction to a line's latitude ∝ its length (used when angles and lengths are equally precise — the normal theodolite-tape case); transit rule — correction ∝ the size of the latitude/departure itself (used when angles are much better than lengths). Numericals 1.2–1.3 run this full pipeline on real numbers; Gale's table (Card 1.12) is simply the tidy register where it all happens.
body.gu:
Latitude અને departure દરેક line ને whole-circle bearing θ અને length L પરથી north-south અને east-west component માં છૂટી પાડે છે:

latitude = L x cos(theta) ; departure = L x sin(theta)

Perfect closed polygon માટે Σlatitude = 0 અને Σdeparture = 0 થવું જોઈએ. જે બાકી રહે તે closing error e = √((Σlat)² + (Σdep)²); accuracy e/perimeter તરીકે કહેવાય છે (1 in 5000 સારું ગણાય). Balancing એ error ને coordinates ગણતા પહેલા વહેંચે છે: Bowditch rule — સુધારો line ની length ના પ્રમાણમાં (angle અને length બંને સરખા precise હોય ત્યારે); transit rule — સુધારો latitude/departure ના મૂલ્યના પ્રમાણમાં (angle વધુ precise હોય ત્યારે). Numerical 1.2–1.3 માં આખી ગણતરી ઉદાહરણ સાથે છે.

items.syllabus_item: 1.12 Gale's Traverse Table and related examples

body.en:
One table, whole computation. Gale's table organises a closed traverse column by column: station and line → observed angle (corrected for angular misclosure first: Σ interior angles must equal (2n−4)×90°) → whole-circle bearing of each line → length → computed latitude and departure (with +/− in separate columns) → corrections by Bowditch rule → corrected latitude/departure → consecutive coordinates (running Σ) → independent coordinates after shifting the start to convenient positive values (often the most-south-west station set to (0,0)-ish, or an assumed 100,100). Its genius is auditability: every column has a checksum — angles close, bearings reverse-check (FB/BB differ by 180°), corrected Σlat and Σdep are exactly zero, and the last station returns to the first station's coordinates.

From table to drawing. Plot by independent coordinates on a grid (never by protractor angles if coordinates exist): the coordinates are the survey, the drawing is their portrait. Areas then fall out by the coordinate (shoelace) method straight from the final columns — the bridge from this unit to area computation everywhere in later surveying.
body.gu:
એક table, આખી ગણતરી: Gale's table column પ્રમાણે ગોઠવાય છે: station/line → angle (પહેલા angular misclosure સુધારો: Σ interior angle = (2n−4)×90°) → દરેક line નો whole-circle bearing → length → latitude અને departure (+/− અલગ column માં) → Bowditch rule થી correction → corrected latitude/departure → consecutive coordinates → પછી independent coordinates (શરૂઆતનું station સુવિધાજનક positive value પર, દા.ત. 100, 100). દરેક column નો checksum છે: corrected Σlat અને Σdep બરાબર શૂન્ય, અને છેલ્લું station પહેલા station ના coordinates પર પાછું આવે.

Table થી drawing: independent coordinates થી grid પર plot કરો — coordinates જ ખરો survey છે, drawing તેનું ચિત્ર છે. Area પણ અંતિમ column પરથી coordinate method થી સીધો મળે છે.

title.en: Closed traverse and Gale's table idea
Numerical 1.1 — Least count and a vernier reading
title.gu: Numerical 1.1 — Least count અને vernier reading

body.en:
Given. A transit theodolite's circle is divided to 20 minutes; its vernier has 60 divisions equal to 59 main-scale divisions. In an observation the vernier index lies just past the main-scale mark 24°40′, and the 18th vernier line coincides. Find the least count and the reading.

Step 1. Least count from its definition.

LC = (1 main-scale division)/(vernier divisions) = 20 min/60 = (20 x 60 sec)/60 = 20 sec

Step 2. Read the main scale up to the division before the index.

main-scale reading = 24 deg 40 min

Step 3. Add the vernier coincidence contribution.

vernier part = 18 x 20 sec = 360 sec = 6 min 00 sec

Final answer.

╔ Reading = 24 deg 46 min 00 sec (least count 20 sec) ╗

Validity check. The seconds part can never reach 60 minutes (60 × 20″ = 20′, exactly one main division) — if your coincidence number implies more, you misread the main scale by one division: the commonest vernier blunder (Card 1.2).
body.gu:
આપેલ છે: circle નો સૌથી નાનો division = 20 minute; vernier ના 60 division = 59 main-scale division. Vernier index 24°40′ ની આગળ છે અને 18મી vernier line coincide થાય છે. Least count અને reading શોધો.

Step 1. Least count ની વ્યાખ્યા પરથી.

LC = 20 min/60 = 20 sec

Step 2. Index પહેલાનો main-scale reading.

main-scale reading = 24 deg 40 min

Step 3. Coincide થતી vernier line નો ફાળો ઉમેરો.

vernier part = 18 x 20 sec = 6 min

અંતિમ જવાબ:

╔ Reading = 24 deg 46 min 00 sec (least count 20 sec) ╗

ચકાસણી: vernier part ક્યારેય 20 minute થી વધે નહીં; વધે તો main scale એક division ખોટો વંચાયો છે — એ જ સૌથી સામાન્ય vernier ભૂલ છે.

title.en: Numerical 1.2 — Latitude, departure and closing error of a closed traverse
title.gu: Numerical 1.2 — Closed traverse ના latitude, departure અને closing error

body.en:
Given. Closed traverse ABCD (whole-circle bearings): AB 100.00 m @ 45°30′; BC 150.40 m @ 122°10′; CD 119.80 m @ 205°05′; DA 189.00 m @ 308°40′. Compute latitudes/departures and the closing error.

Step 1. Apply latitude = L cos θ, departure = L sin θ line by line.

AB: lat = 100.00 cos 45.500 = +70.09 ; dep = 100.00 sin 45.500 = +71.33BC: lat = 150.40 cos 122.167 = -80.07 ; dep = 150.40 sin 122.167 = +127.31CD: lat = 119.80 cos 205.083 = -108.50 ; dep = 119.80 sin 205.083 = -50.79DA: lat = 189.00 cos 308.667 = +118.09 ; dep = 189.00 sin 308.667 = -147.57

Step 2. Sum both columns — a perfect survey would give zero.

sum latitude = -0.40 m ; sum departure = +0.28 m

Step 3. Closing error and relative accuracy (perimeter 559.2 m).

e = sqrt(0.40^2 + 0.28^2) = 0.49 m ; accuracy = 0.49/559.2 = 1 in 1150

Final answer.

╔ Closing error 0.49 m (1 in 1150) - acceptable for an ordinary theodolite traverse; control work demands 1 in 5000 or better ╗

Validity check. Signs follow the bearing's quadrant (NE +, SE lat−/dep+, SW −, NW lat+/dep−). A summation blunder — not field error — is the first suspect whenever the error looks absurd (Card 1.11); Gale's table columns exist to catch exactly that.
body.gu:
આપેલ છે: closed traverse ABCD (whole-circle bearing): AB 100.00 m @ 45°30′; BC 150.40 m @ 122°10′; CD 119.80 m @ 205°05′; DA 189.00 m @ 308°40′. Latitude, departure અને closing error શોધો.

Step 1. દરેક line માટે latitude = L cos θ, departure = L sin θ.

AB: lat +70.09, dep +71.33 ; BC: lat -80.07, dep +127.31 ; CD: lat -108.50, dep -50.79 ; DA: lat +118.09, dep -147.57

Step 2. બંને column નો સરવાળો (perfect survey માં શૂન્ય થવો જોઈએ).

sum latitude = -0.40 m ; sum departure = +0.28 m

Step 3. Closing error અને accuracy (perimeter 559.2 m).

e = sqrt(0.40^2 + 0.28^2) = 0.49 m ; accuracy = 1 in 1150

અંતિમ જવાબ:

╔ Closing error 0.49 m (1 in 1150) — સામાન્ય theodolite traverse માટે ચાલે; control work માટે 1 in 5000 જોઈએ ╗

ચકાસણી: sign bearing ના quadrant પ્રમાણે આવે છે (NE +, SE −/+, SW −, NW +/−).

title.en: Numerical 1.3 — Balancing: angular misclosure and Bowditch corrections
title.gu: Numerical 1.3 — Balancing: angular misclosure અને Bowditch correction

body.en:
Given. Interior angles of the 5-station polygon of the Diagram: A 92°14′20″, B 108°45′40″, C 95°30′10″, D 121°20′30″, E 122°07′40″. Then, for the traverse of Numerical 1.2 (Σlat = −0.40, Σdep = +0.28, perimeter 559.2 m), find the Bowditch correction to line BC (150.40 m).

Step 1. Theoretical sum for n = 5.

sum of interior angles = (2n - 4) x 90 deg = (10 - 4) x 90 = 540 deg 00 min 00 sec

Step 2. Observed sum and misclosure.

observed sum = 539 deg 58 min 20 sec ; misclosure = -1 min 40 sec = -100 sec

Step 3. Distribute equally (angles observed with equal care).

correction per angle = +100/5 = +20 sec (e.g. angle A becomes 92 deg 14 min 40 sec)

Step 4. Bowditch rule for line BC's latitude: correction ∝ length, opposite in sign to the total error.

corr to BC latitude = -(-0.40) x (150.40/559.2) = +0.107 m ; its corrected latitude = -80.07 + 0.11 = -79.96 mcorr to BC departure = -(+0.28) x (150.40/559.2) = -0.075 m ; corrected departure = +127.31 - 0.08 = +127.24 m

Final answer.

╔ Angles corrected +20 sec each; BC balanced to lat -79.96 m, dep +127.24 m - then coordinates close exactly ╗

Validity check. After balancing every line this way, Σ corrected latitudes = Σ corrected departures = 0 by construction; the last station's coordinates must reproduce the first — Gale's table (Card 1.12) ends on that check. Bowditch assumes angles ≈ lengths in precision; transit rule replaces length by the latitude/departure magnitudes when angles are far better (Card 1.11).
body.gu:
આપેલ છે: 5-station polygon ના interior angle: A 92°14′20″, B 108°45′40″, C 95°30′10″, D 121°20′30″, E 122°07′40″. પછી Numerical 1.2 ના traverse (Σlat = −0.40, Σdep = +0.28, perimeter 559.2 m) માટે line BC (150.40 m) નો Bowditch correction શોધો.

Step 1. n = 5 માટે સૈદ્ધાંતિક સરવાળો.

sum = (2n - 4) x 90 deg = 540 deg

Step 2. Observed sum અને misclosure.

observed sum = 539 deg 58 min 20 sec ; misclosure = -100 sec

Step 3. સરખે ભાગે વહેંચો.

દરેક angle નો correction = +20 sec (A = 92 deg 14 min 40 sec)

Step 4. Bowditch rule — correction length ના પ્રમાણમાં, કુલ error થી વિરુદ્ધ sign માં.

BC latitude correction = +0.107 m ; corrected latitude = -79.96 m ; departure correction = -0.075 m ; corrected departure = +127.24 m

અંતિમ જવાબ:

╔ દરેક angle +20 sec સુધાર્યો; BC balance થતાં lat -79.96 m, dep +127.24 m — coordinates બરાબર close થાય છે ╗

ચકાસણી: balancing પછી Σ corrected latitude = Σ corrected departure = 0 જ થાય; છેલ્લું station પહેલા station ના coordinates પર પાછું આવવું જોઈએ — Gale's table (Card 1.12) આ check પર પૂરું થાય છે.

title.en: Formulae, methods and key data — Unit 1
title.gu: Formulae, methods અને key data — યુનિટ 1

name.en: Angles, vernier and traverse closure arithmetic
name.gu: Angle, vernier અને traverse closure ની ગણતરી

body.en:
least count = (1 main-scale division)/(vernier divisions) ; transit theodolite: 20 min/60 = 20 sec (N1.1)reading = main-scale reading (before index) + coinciding vernier division x LC ; mean of verniers A and B cancels eccentricitysum of interior angles of closed polygon = (2n - 4) x 90 deg ; permissible angular misclosure approx sqrt(n) x LC, distributed equally (N1.3)latitude = L cos(WCB) ; departure = L sin(WCB) ; closing error e = sqrt((sum lat)^2 + (sum dep)^2) ; accuracy = e/perimeter (N1.2)

Every traverse number flows: angles → bearings → latitude/departure → closure → balance → coordinates. A break anywhere shows up in the next column's checksum.
body.gu:
least count = (1 main-scale division)/(vernier divisions) ; transit theodolite: 20 min/60 = 20 sec (Numerical 1.1)reading = main-scale reading + coinciding vernier division x LC ; vernier A અને B નું mean eccentricity cancel કરે છેinterior angles નો સરવાળો = (2n - 4) x 90 deg ; angular misclosure approx sqrt(n) x LC, સરખે ભાગે વહેંચાય (Numerical 1.3)latitude = L cos(WCB) ; departure = L sin(WCB) ; closing error e = sqrt((sum lat)^2 + (sum dep)^2) ; accuracy = e/perimeter (Numerical 1.2)

દરેક traverse number આ ક્રમમાં વહે છે: angles → bearings → latitude/departure → closure → balance → coordinates.

name.en: Balancing rules and field tolerances — data bank
name.gu: Balancing rules અને field tolerances — data bank

body.en:
Bowditch (compass) rule: correction to latitude of a line = -total lat error x (line length/perimeter) - angles and lengths equally trusted (standard for theodolite + tape)transit rule: correction = -total lat error x (line latitude/sum of absolute latitudes) - when angles are much better than lengthsface-left + face-right mean cancels: collimation error, trunnion-axis tilt, vertical index error ; A/B vernier mean cancels eccentricityrepetition: angle measured n times, divided by n - precision improves roughly n times ; reiteration: close horizon = 360 deg check at a station

Rule of thumb viva line: adjust the instrument rarely, observe so errors cancel always, and never balance a blunder — re-observe it.
body.gu:
Bowditch rule: latitude correction = -કુલ error x (line length/perimeter) — angle અને length બંને સરખા trusted હોય ત્યારે (theodolite + tape માટે standard)transit rule: correction = -કુલ error x (line latitude/કુલ absolute latitudes) — angle, length કરતાં વધુ precise હોય ત્યારેface-left + face-right mean થી cancel: collimation error, trunnion tilt, index error ; A/B vernier mean થી eccentricity cancelrepetition: angle n વખત માપી n થી ભાગવો — precision લગભગ n ગણી ; reiteration: station પર horizon = 360 deg check

Viva માટે યાદ રાખો: instrument ભાગ્યે જ adjust કરો, પણ observation હંમેશા એવી ગોઠવો કે error cancel થાય; blunder ક્યારેય balance ન કરો — ફરી observe કરો.

q.en: Why is the instrument called a 'transit' theodolite?
q.gu: આ instrument ને 'transit' theodolite કેમ કહે છે?

a.en: Because its telescope can be transited — flipped a full 180° about the trunnion (horizontal) axis. That single property enables face-left/face-right observing, prolonging lines, and most error cancellation in Unit 1.
a.gu: કારણ કે telescope trunnion axis પર સંપૂર્ણ 180° flip (transit) થઈ શકે છે. એ એક જ property થી face-left/face-right observation, line prolong અને મોટાભાગની error cancellation શક્ય બને છે.

q.en: Least count 20 seconds — show where it comes from, don't quote it.
q.gu: Least count 20 second — ક્યાંથી આવે છે તે બતાવો, ખાલી કહો નહીં.

a.en: One main-scale division is 20 minutes = 1200 seconds; the vernier splits it into 60 parts; 1200/60 = 20 seconds. Change either number and the least count changes (Numerical 1.1).
a.gu: એક main-scale division = 20 minute = 1200 second; vernier તેને 60 ભાગમાં વહેંચે છે; 1200/60 = 20 second. બેમાંથી એક number બદલાય તો least count બદલાય (Numerical 1.1).

q.en: Temporary adjustment order at a station?
q.gu: Station પર temporary adjustment નો ક્રમ?

a.en: Set up and centre, level with the foot screws, then focus (eyepiece first, then objective, killing parallax). Centering after levelling destroys the level; parallax left in becomes pointing error at every target.
a.gu: પહેલા centering, પછી foot screw થી levelling, પછી focussing (પહેલા eyepiece, પછી objective — parallax દૂર કરીને). Levelling પછી centering કરશો તો level બગડશે; parallax રહેશે તો દરેક target પર pointing error આવશે.

q.en: Which errors does a face-left/face-right mean cancel?
q.gu: Face-left/face-right mean કઈ errors cancel કરે છે?

a.en: Collimation error (sight line not perpendicular to trunnion axis), trunnion-axis tilt (not perpendicular to vertical axis) and vertical-circle index error — all reverse sign on changing face, so the mean is clean.
a.gu: Collimation error, trunnion-axis tilt અને vertical-circle index error — ત્રણેય face બદલતાં sign બદલે છે, એટલે mean શુદ્ધ મળે છે.

q.en: Repetition versus reiteration in one line each.
q.gu: Repetition vs reiteration એક-એક line માં.

a.en: Repetition: the same angle added n times and divided by n — precision for one important angle. Reiteration: all angles around a station measured in sequence closing the horizon at 360° — control for a radiating station.
a.gu: Repetition: એ જ angle n વખત ઉમેરી n થી ભાગવો — એક મહત્વના angle માટે precision. Reiteration: station આસપાસના બધા angle ક્રમમાં માપી horizon 360° પર close કરવો — ઘણી line વાળા station માટે control.

q.en: The plate bubble stays centred at 0° but not after a 180° swing. Diagnosis?
q.gu: Plate bubble 0° પર centre છે પણ 180° swing પછી નથી. કારણ?

a.en: Plate-bubble axis is not perpendicular to the vertical axis — a permanent-adjustment fault. Halve the displacement with the bubble's adjusting screws, re-level, repeat; field work-around is careful relevelling at each pointing.
a.gu: Plate-bubble axis, vertical axis ને perpendicular નથી — permanent-adjustment ની ખામી. Bubble ના adjusting screw થી અડધો ફેરફાર સુધારો, ફરી level કરો; field માં દરેક pointing પહેલા re-level કરવું એ ઉપાય છે.

q.en: Fore bearing of AB is 45°30′; back bearing measured 225°50′. Comment.
q.gu: AB નો fore bearing 45°30′; back bearing 225°50′ મળ્યો. ટિપ્પણી કરો.

a.en: They must differ by exactly 180° (expected BB 225°30′). The 20′ discrepancy at one end signals local attraction (or a misread vernier) — trust neither station's needle until checked with a clean station pair.
a.gu: બંને વચ્ચે બરાબર 180° હોવું જોઈએ (expected 225°30′). 20′ નો ફરક local attraction અથવા vernier misreading સૂચવે છે — બીજી station જોડી સાથે check કર્યા વગર વિશ્વાસ ન કરો.

q.en: Why two verniers, A and B, 180° apart?
q.gu: બે vernier A અને B 180° દૂર કેમ હોય છે?

a.en: Eccentricity: if the circle's centre and the rotation axis do not coincide, one vernier reads high where the other reads low by the same amount; the mean of A and B cancels it.
a.gu: Eccentricity ને કારણે: circle નું centre અને rotation axis ન મળે તો એક vernier જેટલું વધુ વાંચે તેટલું જ બીજું ઓછું વાંચે; બંનેનું mean error cancel કરે છે.

q.en: Bowditch or transit rule for your theodolite-and-tape traverse? Defend.
q.gu: તમારા theodolite + tape traverse માટે Bowditch કે transit rule? બચાવ કરો.

a.en: Bowditch: it assumes angular and linear measurements carry comparable precision — true for a 20″ theodolite with careful taping. Transit rule only when angles are demonstrably much better than the lengths (Numerical 1.3).
a.gu: Bowditch: angle અને length બંનેની precision લગભગ સરખી ધારે છે — 20″ theodolite અને કાળજીપૂર્વકના taping માટે સાચું છે. Transit rule ફક્ત angle, length કરતાં નોંધપાત્ર સારા હોય ત્યારે (Numerical 1.3).

q.en: Your polygon's angles sum to 539°58′20″ for five stations. Reaction?
q.gu: પાંચ station ના polygon ના angles નો સરવાળો 539°58′20″ આવ્યો. તમારી પ્રતિક્રિયા?

a.en: Expected (2×5−4)×90° = 540°, so misclosure is −1′40″, inside √(5)×20″-style tolerance scaled for the set: distribute +20″ per angle before computing bearings — but a misclosure beyond tolerance means re-observe, not distribute (Numerical 1.3).
a.gu: Expected (2×5−4)×90° = 540°, એટલે misclosure −1′40″ છે; tolerance માં હોય તો દરેક angle પર +20″ વહેંચી bearing ગણો — પણ tolerance બહાર હોય તો વહેંચવાનું નહીં, ફરી observe કરવાનું (Numerical 1.3).

q.en: Deflection angle is booked '12°30′ R'. What does the line do?
q.gu: Deflection angle '12°30′ R' નોંધાયો છે. Line શું કરે છે?

a.en: It turns 12°30′ to the right (clockwise) from the prolongation of the incoming line. Without the R the next party can mirror your road; with it, the alignment is unambiguous (Card 1.8).
a.gu: Line અગાઉની line ના prolongation થી જમણી બાજુ (clockwise) 12°30′ વળે છે. R ન લખો તો બીજી party road ને mirror કરી નાખી શકે; R લખવાથી alignment સ્પષ્ટ રહે છે.

q.en: Why not just tape the coordinates of stations directly and skip angles?
q.gu: Angles છોડીને ફક્ત tape થી coordinates કેમ ન માપવા?

a.en: Coordinates come FROM angles + lengths: a tape alone gives distances with no directions — an infinity of polygons fit the same five lengths. The theodolite supplies the directions that make the framework rigid; Gale's table turns both into coordinates.
a.gu: Coordinates angle + length બંનેથી જ બને છે: એકલું tape distance આપે, direction નહીં — એ જ પાંચ length પર અનંત polygon બની શકે. Theodolite direction આપી framework ને rigid બનાવે છે; Gale's table બંનેને coordinates માં ફેરવે છે.

q.en: Draw a neat labelled sketch of a transit vernier theodolite, name its parts, and state the uses of a theodolite.
q.gu: Transit vernier theodolite નો સ્વચ્છ નામવાળો sketch દોરો, parts ના નામ આપો અને theodolite ના ઉપયોગ જણાવો.

q.en: Explain the temporary adjustments of a theodolite in order. What are the fundamental axes, and what relations must hold between them in perfect adjustment?
q.gu: Theodolite ના temporary adjustment ક્રમમાં સમજાવો. Fundamental axes કયા છે અને perfect adjustment માં તેમની વચ્ચે કયા સંબંધો હોવા જોઈએ?

q.en: Explain the repetition and reiteration methods of measuring a horizontal angle. How is a vertical angle measured, and how does face-left/face-right observing remove index error?
q.gu: Horizontal angle માપવાની repetition અને reiteration method સમજાવો. Vertical angle કેવી રીતે મપાય છે, અને face-left/face-right observation index error કેવી રીતે દૂર કરે છે?

q.en: Describe the errors in theodolite work (instrumental, personal, natural) and the field precautions or observation schemes that eliminate each.
q.gu: Theodolite work ની errors (instrumental, personal, natural) અને દરેકને દૂર કરવાની field સાવચેતી/observation રીત વર્ણવો.

q.en: With the whole-circle bearings and lengths of a 4-sided closed traverse (data as in class example), compute latitudes, departures and the closing error, and state the relative accuracy.
q.gu: 4 બાજુવાળા closed traverse ના whole-circle bearing અને length (class example મુજબ data) પરથી latitude, departure અને closing error ગણો અને relative accuracy જણાવો.

q.en: What is Gale's traverse table? List its columns in order and the check available at each stage, ending with independent coordinates.
q.gu: Gale's traverse table શું છે? તેના columns ક્રમમાં લખો અને દરેક stage પર મળતો check, છેલ્લે independent coordinates સુધી, જણાવો.

q.en: Distinguish between: (a) transiting and swinging, (b) face left and face right, (c) direct angle and deflection angle, (d) Bowditch rule and transit rule.
q.gu: તફાવત આપો: (a) transiting અને swinging, (b) face left અને face right, (c) direct angle અને deflection angle, (d) Bowditch rule અને transit rule.

q.en: (a) A vernier has 60 divisions equal to 59 main divisions of 20 minutes — find the least count and the reading when the index is past 24°40′ with the 18th line coinciding. (b) The interior angles of a 5-station polygon sum to 539°58′20″ — find the correction per angle.
q.gu: (a) Vernier ના 60 division = 59 main division (દરેક 20 minute) છે — least count શોધો અને index 24°40′ ની આગળ તથા 18મી line coincide થતી હોય ત્યારે reading શોધો. (b) 5-station polygon ના interior angles નો સરવાળો 539°58′20″ છે — દરેક angle નો correction શોધો.
